To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 2010 report on PR deposits by IFDC has had a profound influence on the PR scarcity debate and that it appears to present a significantly inflated picture of PR reserves, in particular of those of Morocco.

(i) the IFDC report does not use the thresholds for reserves and (ii) resources used by the USGS and other leading mineral resource classification systems; (iii) it is not clear whether IFDC's terminology is likely to yield comparable, reliable and credible data; (iv) the difference between raw PR ore deposits and upgraded PR concentrate should be noted in the literature; and (v) the report may present an inflated picture of reserves and resources, in particular for Morocco.

the recent increase in global PR reserves is due to a single report, the IFDC report of 2010, which used an unorthodox terminology for reserves and resources and which has been used to report reserves and resources in the literature since then.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quality and credibility of data on global PR reserves and resources, as reported by the IFDC.
the question of whether the IFDC's 2010 report has provided a credible and transparent basis for the debate on the scarcity of PR and its impact on food production.
the reliability and credibility of data on PR deposits and their potential for future extraction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no reliable information on the global PR resource base.

, while PR is not scarce in the sense of running out in the near future, there is a need for a more detailed analysis of the global PR situation, including the development of an agreed-upon terminology for PR resources and reserves.

there is no evidence that global PR reserves and resources have increased significantly in recent years, and that the data currently available do not warrant the conclusion that global PR deposits are likely to last thousands of years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data on which the statements of PR scarcity are based are not sufficiently transparent, comparable, and reliable.
the IFDC report has not provided a solution to the problem of the scarcity of phosphate rock.
the current debate on the availability of phosphate rock is not based on reliable and comparable data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is a need to develop a consensus terminology for reporting PR reserves and resources, and that this should include clear thresholds for reserves, resources, and reserves-to-resources conversion.
there is a clear need to improve the reporting of data on PR deposits.

the PR scarcity debate has been shifted from resource scarcity to pollution, and that the debate on the latter should be informed by accurate and reliable data on PR reserves, resources, consumption, and pollution.
